title: Business plan outline for a cleaning business (editable template)
audience: Owners who are writing or rewriting a written business plan for a cleaning business, and who need each section to agree with the others
learningOutcomes: Complete each section of the plan in the order that lets later sections depend on earlier decisions
Write the executive summary last, using only statements that appear in the sections
Record the review date, version and reviewer, so that the plan is maintained rather than filed and forgotten

instruction.heading: What this plan is and what it is not
instruction.body: A business plan records the decisions behind a business and tests whether they fit together. It is not a sales document, and it does not replace the financial projections that an accountant or adviser prepares. This template follows the general shape of a plan: a summary, the business, its services and customers, the market and competitors, the marketing and pricing approach, the operations and team, the finances, the milestones and risks, and the attachments. It poses questions under every heading and does not supply answers. The earlier lessons explain how to answer them: “How a cleaning business plan is structured” covers the structure, “Customer needs and building trust in a cleaning business” customer needs, “SWOT analysis for a small cleaning business” the SWOT analysis, “Break-even and sales forecast by stage” break-even and forecasting, and “Staffing in stages: the first team, then new teams” staffing. This lesson refers to those lessons and does not repeat them. The market and competitor sections are completed in more depth in “Market, customer and competitor analysis”, the pricing in “Pricing and margin worksheet”, the break-even worksheet in “Freedom and cash plan”, and the marketing channels in “Marketing plan”.

instruction.heading: The order in which to write it
instruction.body: Write the sections in the order that the decisions depend on each other. Start with the services and the customers, because every later number depends on what is sold and to whom. Then complete the market and competitor summary from “Market, customer and competitor analysis”, followed by the pricing and marketing approach. The operations and team come next, because the number of jobs a team can deliver sets the revenue that is possible. The financial targets and break-even come after that, and the funding need comes last among the financial sections. The executive summary and the mission are written last, because they can only summarise decisions that already exist. A plan written in the opposite order tends to fit its numbers to its story.

instruction.heading: Facts, targets and assumptions
instruction.body: Label each number. A fact is observed or recorded. A target is a goal the owner sets. An assumption is a belief that a target depends on, and it needs a date and a way to test it. An overseas or historical figure is labelled as historical and is not used as a current Australian figure. Where a figure cannot yet be sourced, write that it is not yet sourced and say what would confirm it. A reader should be able to tell, for every number in the plan, which of the three it is.

instruction.heading: Keeping the plan alive
instruction.body: Set a review date and a version number. When a figure, a service or a price changes, record the old value, the new value, the reason and the date, rather than overwriting the history. A plan that is reviewed once and then left stops matching the business. Name the person responsible for the next review, so the date is not left to chance.

instruction.heading: What the plan cannot settle
instruction.body: Registration, licences, insurance, tax obligations and employment status depend on the work done and on the state or territory where it is done. The plan states each of them as a question to be checked, until a source has been checked and recorded. A plan that presents an unchecked legal or tax position as settled will mislead its owner and anyone who reads it.

procedure: Enter the trading name and any legal name that differs, the state or territory of registration, and the version and review date.
Write the mission in one or two sentences that name the work, the customer and the result.
Describe the business's location, start date and legal structure.
List each service in the table with what is included, what is excluded, the typical job length and the pricing basis.
Describe each customer segment by who decides, what they buy and how often, referring to the analysis in “Market, customer and competitor analysis”.
Summarise the market and competitor findings in five sentences or fewer, each traceable to “Market, customer and competitor analysis”.
Name the marketing channels and the segment each one reaches, referring to “Marketing plan”.
State the pricing method and refer to the pricing and margin worksheet (“Pricing and margin worksheet”), without entering an unconfirmed price.
Describe the daily operations, the scheduling method, the sign-off steps and the tools and vehicles used.
Complete the team table, with each hire linked to a demand trigger from “Staffing in stages: the first team, then new teams”.
Enter the financial targets, with jobs, average job value, revenue and the checked date for each assumption.
Write the break-even and cash flow section, referring to “Freedom and cash plan”, and state the funding need and its uses.
Complete the milestones and risks tables, with each risk tied to a named response and owner.
List the attachments and sources with their check dates, then write the executive summary last and check each of its statements against a section.

workedExamples.situation: A solo owner writes the customers section as middle and upper-income homeowners, and the pricing section as a premium service at a premium price.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which entries must be defined before the financial targets can be checked, and how should they be rewritten?
workedExamples.reasoning: An income band is a claim to be tested, not a starting definition. It should be replaced with who decides, what they buy and how often they buy, so the sales channel and the job frequency can be estimated. The premium price is a position, not a price. The pricing section needs the basis, such as the hours, the rate and the margin, and the job size it applies to. Until both sections are defined, the number of jobs and the average job value cannot be linked, so the break-even figure in the financial section cannot be checked.

equipmentAndPpe: Dated notes from local market observation, as set out in “Market, customer and competitor analysis”
Pricing and margin worksheet (“Pricing and margin worksheet”) and break-even worksheet (“Freedom and cash plan”)
List of decisions made so far, for cross-checking the sections
Source list with check dates for any market, regulatory or tax statement
PPE: not applicable to this lesson; the plan is a document

commonErrors.error: Writing the executive summary first, then fitting the sections to match it.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the summary last, and check each of its statements against a section of the plan.

commonErrors.error: Defining customers by a general demographic label.
commonErrors.prevention: Define each segment by who decides, what they buy and how often they buy, with evidence from “Market, customer and competitor analysis”.

commonErrors.error: Stating a financial target with no jobs or average job value shown.
commonErrors.prevention: Every target shows the number of jobs, the average job value, the revenue and the assumption that links them.

commonErrors.error: Presenting an overseas or historical figure as a current Australian fact.
commonErrors.prevention: Label it as historical or overseas, with its source and year, and keep it out of the targets.

commonErrors.error: Listing generic risks that could apply to any business.
commonErrors.prevention: Tie each risk to a service, customer, supplier or season in this business, and name a response the business can carry out.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Registration, licences, insurance and tax obligations for a cleaning business depend on the work and on the state or territory. This template does not set them. Confirm with the relevant authority or a qualified adviser.
Check legal structure, employment or contractor status, and the application of the Privacy Act 1988 to the business with the relevant regulator before relying on this point.

For GST, the ATO sets the registration threshold at $75,000 of GST turnover for most businesses, and $150,000 a year or more for non-profit organisations (ATO page last updated 14 September 2026). Whether this business must register is a check against its own turnover and must be confirmed with the ATO. Take advice from a qualified adviser before relying on any figure in the financial section.
This lesson does not grant a licence, certificate, registration or authority of any kind. Completing the plan does not confirm that the business may trade.

qualityStandard: Every section is completed, or marked not applicable with a reason
Mission, services, customers, pricing and targets use the same definitions as “Pricing and margin worksheet” and “Market, customer and competitor analysis”
Every financial target shows jobs, average job value and an assumption with its check date
Every statement in the executive summary can be traced to a section of the plan
Each statement still to be checked carries a named owner for its check
documentationEvidence: Completed plan saved with its version number, date and review date
Change log for each figure changed after the first version
Sources and check dates for each market, regulatory and tax statement
Name of the person responsible for the next review
summary: A plan is a set of linked decisions, and the template checks that they agree.
Write the executive summary last, from the sections.
Every number is labelled as a fact, a target or an assumption.
Legal, tax and registration statements stay out until they are checked.

editableTemplates.title: Business plan
editableTemplates.purpose: A written plan with sections for the summary, the business, its services and customers, the market and competitors (completed in “Market, customer and competitor analysis”), marketing and pricing, operations and team, finances, funding, milestones and risks, and attachments, with a version and a review date.

fields.label: Trading name and legal name
fields.prompt: Write the trading name, and the legal name if it differs. Note the state or territory where the business is registered.
fields.guidance: Both names match the registration documents held. Where registration has not been checked, the field is left blank.

fields.label: Version, date and reviewer
fields.prompt: Enter the version number, the date of this version and the name of the person who reviews the plan.
fields.guidance: The version changes with each review. The reviewer is named, not a role only.

fields.label: Mission
fields.prompt: Write one or two sentences that name the work, the customer and the result the customer gets.
fields.guidance: Each part of the mission can be found later in the services and customers sections.

fields.label: Business description and history
fields.prompt: Describe where the business is based, when it started trading, its legal structure, and any partnership or alliance.
fields.guidance: Dates are actual dates. The legal structure is left blank if it has not been checked.

fields.label: Services
fields.prompt: One row per service. Columns: service, what is included, what is excluded, typical job length, pricing basis.
fields.guidance: Inclusions and exclusions are specific enough to price against. Job length is marked as an estimate where it is not measured. The pricing basis refers to “Pricing and margin worksheet”.

fields.label: Customer segments
fields.prompt: One row per customer segment. Columns: segment, who decides, what they buy, how often they buy. The full analysis is in “Market, customer and competitor analysis”.
fields.guidance: Each segment names the decision maker and the frequency. An income band may be a note but is not the definition.

fields.label: Market and competitor summary
fields.prompt: Summarise the market and competitor findings in five sentences or fewer, referring to the completed “Market, customer and competitor analysis” analysis.
fields.guidance: Every statement matches “Market, customer and competitor analysis” and carries a date, or is marked as the author's observation.

fields.label: Marketing approach
fields.prompt: Name the main channels and the segment each one reaches, referring to the marketing plan (“Marketing plan”).
fields.guidance: The channels match the customer segments in the customers table.

fields.label: Pricing approach
fields.prompt: State the pricing method and refer to the pricing and margin worksheet (“Pricing and margin worksheet”). Do not enter a price that has not been confirmed.
fields.guidance: Names the method and the worksheet. Price figures come from the worksheet, not from this plan.

fields.label: Operations
fields.prompt: Describe the daily operations: how jobs are scheduled, how the team arrives, how work is signed off, and which tools and vehicles are used.
fields.guidance: Matches the scheduling method in the business settings and the sign-off steps in the job records.

fields.label: Team and hiring
fields.prompt: One row per role. Columns: role, who fills it now, experience relevant to the role, next hire, and the demand trigger for that hire.
fields.guidance: Each hire is linked to a demand trigger (“Staffing in stages: the first team, then new teams”). A role is not left blank without a reason.

fields.label: Financial targets
fields.prompt: One row per period. Columns: period, jobs, average job value, revenue target, assumptions, date each assumption was checked.
fields.guidance: Revenue equals jobs multiplied by average job value. Each assumption has a check date.

fields.label: Break-even and cash flow
fields.prompt: State the monthly fixed costs, the break-even job count, and how cash comes in and goes out. Refer to the worksheet in “Freedom and cash plan”.
fields.guidance: Break-even links to “Freedom and cash plan”. Timing gaps between work done and money received are named. Tax and superannuation treatment has not yet been confirmed, so check with the relevant regulator before relying on this point.

fields.label: Funding requirement and use
fields.prompt: State how much money is needed to start or run the business, where it comes from, and its main uses.
fields.guidance: Each use has an amount and a basis. Any source of funds is named. The figure comes from a calculation, not an untested estimate.

fields.label: Risks and responses
fields.prompt: One row per risk. Columns: risk, likelihood (low, medium or high), response, owner, review date.
fields.guidance: Each risk is specific to this business and each response is something the business can do. Link to the SWOT (“SWOT analysis for a small cleaning business”) where it was used.

fields.label: Milestones
fields.prompt: One row per milestone. Columns: milestone, date, measure of success.
fields.guidance: Milestones are dated and measurable, such as a count of recurring clients reached by a date.

fields.label: Management team gaps
fields.prompt: Name the roles still needed for the plan to work, and the date each one is needed.
fields.guidance: Each gap has a date and a reason. A gap is named even if an adviser or contractor will fill it.

fields.label: Attachments and sources
fields.prompt: List each attachment, such as the worksheets and market sources, with its date.
fields.guidance: Every attachment is listed, and each source has its check date.

fields.label: Executive summary
fields.prompt: Write this section last. Summarise what the business sells, to whom, where, and what it needs to work, in a short paragraph.
fields.guidance: Every statement can be traced to a section of this plan. No statement appears here that is missing from the body.

levels.meets: Mission, services, customers, pricing and targets use the same definitions and do not contradict each other.
levels.does_not_meet: A figure or definition in one section contradicts another section, with no explanation.

levels.meets: Each revenue target equals jobs multiplied by average job value, and each assumption has a check date.
levels.does_not_meet: A target has no jobs, no average value, or an assumption with no date.

levels.meets: Each segment names who decides, what they buy and how often.
levels.does_not_meet: A segment is described only by a demographic label or an income band.

levels.meets: Every statement in the summary traces to a section of the plan.
levels.does_not_meet: The summary makes a claim that does not appear in the body.

assessmentRubric.criterion: Statements still to be checked are owned

levels.meets: Each legal, tax, registration or regulatory statement is either checked and sourced, or left out with a named owner.
levels.does_not_meet: A legal, tax or registration statement is presented as settled without a source.

officialReferences.title: Small business and the Privacy Act (OAIC)
officialReferences.covers: Defines a small business as one with annual turnover of $3 million or less, and says most small businesses are not covered by the Privacy Act but some are, including some regardless of turnover (for example health service providers and businesses trading in personal information). Does not settle whether this particular business is covered, so that point stays not yet confirmed until checked. Publisher: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner. Read through a summary fetch in this pass, not checked against the page text directly.

officialReferences.title: Registering for GST (Australian Taxation Office)
officialReferences.pageDate: Last updated 14 September 2026 (the page was last updated on that date)
officialReferences.covers: Read directly on 2026-11-03. States the GST registration threshold: $75,000 of GST turnover for other businesses, and $150,000 per year or more for non-profit organisations; registration must be done within 21 days once required. Does not address income tax, superannuation, owner drawings or the GST rate, which remain not yet confirmed. Publisher: Australian Taxation Office.
